Analytic replay: use the determinant lemma on the rank-one covariance feedback, the displayed impulse coefficients and Euler's terminating hypergeometric transformation; use the same feedback on the continuous covariance generator with return kernel G e^(−2t)t^(2n)/(n!)².
correctness.rationale: On symmetric second moments the update is Φ(C)=TCTᵀ+hσ²C₁₁e_me_mᵀ. Rank-one initial matrices span the symmetric space, so decay for every deterministic input is equivalent to spectral radius below one. For h≥2 Jensen on the mean with initial state e₁ rules out decay. For 0<h<2 the unforced spectral radius is (1−h)². The resolvent feedback series for real λ above this radius is strictly decreasing from infinity to zero; at h=1 it is a single nonzero inverse-power term. The unique feedback root is an eigenvalue and no larger modulus can satisfy the feedback equation, since the absolute value of the complex series is bounded by the positive series at its modulus. The response coefficient is binom(k,n)(1−h)^(k−n)(κh)^n for k≥n. Euler's identity for the binomial-square series and 1−(1−h)²=h(2−h) give the stated gain at λ=1 and show that equality is not asymptotically stable. For continuous time the rank-one resolvent feedback is G binom(2n,n)/(s+2)^(2n+1) in Re(s)>−2, so its positive-real-axis-side root s=−2+[G binom(2n,n)]^(1/(2n+1)) has maximal real part. With r=1−h, on r≤0 the numerator (1+r)^(2n+1) increases and P_n(r²) decreases. For r>0 the denominator after factoring (1+r)^(2n) is a binomial collision probability whose Fourier integral strictly decreases as r/(1+r) increases. These pieces join continuously and yield strict monotonicity on the whole interval, the stated endpoint limits, and precisely one crossing when G<G_c,n.
residual_risks: The packaged spectral comparisons are finite numerical diagnostics (and do not test equality cases as spectral decisions); stability at arbitrary dimension and the strict critical exclusion follow from the analytic feedback argument. Assumes independent centered increments of variance h and one closing multiplicative noise.

value.rationale: This is a natural feedback family: a nonnormal deterministic shift transfers the noise injection back to its sensing coordinate, and mean stability can coexist with mean-square numerical instability. The result replaces a dimension-growing covariance spectral test with an explicit one-parameter polynomial threshold that decides every step for any chain length, and supplies the exact continuous/discrete comparison. General Lyapunov step nesting is useful background but is not itself the contribution.
residual_risks: Specific to one chain and one noise direction, with no assertion about other integrators or arbitrary nonnormal systems.
